newsitem.title: INDIA: India ITC down nine pct in afternoon.
newsitem.headline: India ITC down nine pct in afternoon.

text.p: Shares of tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC Ltd dropped 47.0 rupees, or 8.8 percent, to 488.0 at the Bombay exchange in Monday afternoon deals, traders said.
Traders did not attribute the stock's sharp fall to any particular reason. Rumours that a foreign fund had booked profits in ITC might be pulling the stock lower, they said.
The stock topped the list of most heavily traded stocks traded at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
"ITC is in the grip of speculators. There has not been any news to lead to such a big reaction," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
The firm on Saturday set a dividend of four rupees per share for the year 1996/97 against 2.50 rupees in the previous year.

Shares of ITC were put under price limits at the National Stock Exchange at 496.80 as the counter saw only sellers in the stock. Total sell orders totalled over 500,000 shares when the stock was put under a price-limit, traders said.
ITC has rocketed 75 percent in 1997 as players bought into the stock based on good performance in 1996/97 (March-April).
The tobacco and hotel conglomerate had posted a 33 percent growth in net profit to 3.47 billion rupees from 2.61 billion rupees the previous year.
ITC Ltd is 31.7 percent owned by Britain's B.A.T. Industries plc.
